title: Michael Gray, Star of 1970s 'Shazam!' Series, Dies at 75
dek: The actor who portrayed Billy Batson on the live-action 'Shazam!' series from 1974 to 1976 died in Palm Desert, California, with tributes noting his later cameo in the 2023 film sequel.
metaDescription: Michael Gray, who played Billy Batson on the 1970s 'Shazam!' TV series, died October 16, 2026 in Palm Desert, California at age 75.

sections.heading: Death and Career-Defining Role
sections.body: Michael Gray, who starred as Billy Batson on the 1970s live-action television series "Shazam!" died on October 16, 2026 in Palm Desert, California at age 75, according to multiple outlets [1][2][3]. The series aired for three seasons from 1974 to 1976 on CBS [1][2][3]. Gray's Billy Batson traveled the country in a recreational vehicle with Mentor, played by Les Tremayne, encountering people in need of help; when trouble arose, Billy would speak the magic word "Shazam!" to transform into Captain Marvel, portrayed first by Jackson Bostwick and then by John Davey [1][2][3]. The show became a Saturday-morning staple and defined Gray's public identity for decades.

sections.heading: Early Television Work and Teen Idol Status
sections.body: Before landing "Shazam!" Gray appeared in several notable television productions. He had an onscreen debut on a 1969 episode of "Room 222" according to The Hollywood Reporter [3], and appeared in the 1970 ABC telefilm "Run, Simon, Run" alongside Burt Reynolds per Variety and The Hollywood Reporter [2][3]. In 1972 he was cast as student doctor Ronnie Collins on NBC's "The Little People" alongside Brian Keith and Shelley Fabares [1][2][3]. A 1973 episode of "The Brady Bunch" featured Gray as Marcia's boyfriend [1][2][3]. Variety and The Hollywood Reporter describe Gray as a teen idol during this period, noting he was managed by Charles Laufer, publisher of Tiger Beat, and that the attention became overwhelming [2][3]. Gray told The Hollywood Reporter in a later interview: "They wanted me to be the next David Cassidy... I couldn't leave my house. It got pretty ugly sometimes" [3].

sections.heading: Hiatus, Return, and Later Appearances
sections.body: After "Shazam!" ended, Gray stepped away from acting for an extended period. Variety and The Hollywood Reporter report that he felt typecast and worked in children's theater education, men's fashion, and co-owned a floral business with his wife Stacy [2][3]. He married Stacy Benon Gray in 1994 [2][3]. A career resurgence began around 2012 when "Shazam!" was remastered for DVD release [2][3]. From 2015 to 2019 Gray voiced a fictionalized version of himself, "TV's Michael Gray," on four episodes of the animated series "Archer" [1][2][3]. He also appeared in the independent "Surge of Power" franchise; The Hollywood Reporter specifies he voiced the character Will E. Bee from 2016 to 2020 [3]. In 2023 Gray made a cameo in "Shazam! Fury of the Gods" interacting with Zachary Levi's Captain Marvel [1][2][3].

sections.heading: Tributes and Disputed Biographical Details
sections.body: Former co-star John Davey told Variety: "From my very first day on Shazam!, Mike and Les [Tremayne] welcomed me like a king... Mike was a wonderful man. I don't think he ever stopped smiling" [2]. The Hollywood Reporter carries a similar but different quote from Davey [3]. Gray himself reflected on the show's impact in a 2012 Fanboy Planet interview, saying: "I meet people [everyday] who say, You have no idea what you did for me as a child... You made me the better man, or woman, that I am today" [2]; The Hollywood Reporter attributes a longer version of this quote to the same interview [3]. Regarding biographical details, Variety and The Hollywood Reporter state Gray was born September 2, 1951 in Chicago and raised in Miami Beach, Florida, and studied at the Pasadena Playhouse [2][3]; Rolling Stone does not include these details [1]. Variety reports the cause of death as natural causes [2]; Rolling Stone does not specify a cause [1]. Variety lists survivors as wife Stacy Benon Gray, step-children Ryan Cooper and Laurel Cooper, and son-in-law Lee Barker [2]; The Hollywood Reporter mentions wife, stepchildren Ryan and Cooper, and son-in-law Lee with slightly different names [3]; Rolling Stone does not mention survivors [1].

keyTakeaways: Michael Gray, star of the 1974-1976 'Shazam!' TV series as Billy Batson, died October 16, 2026 in Palm Desert, California at age 75.
The series ran three seasons; Captain Marvel was played by Jackson Bostwick then John Davey, with Les Tremayne as Mentor.
Gray's later career included a 2023 cameo in 'Shazam! Fury of the Gods' with Zachary Levi and voice work on 'Archer' (2015-2019).
Biographical details including birth date, birthplace, upbringing, and cause of death appear in Variety and Hollywood Reporter but not Rolling Stone.
Survivor information varies between outlets: Variety and Hollywood Reporter list wife Stacy and stepchildren with slightly different names.
whyItMatters: Gray's death marks the end of a direct link to the first live-action adaptation of the Captain Marvel/Shazam character, a series that introduced the hero to a generation of television viewers. His later cameo in the 2023 film created a rare bridge between the 1970s series and the modern DC cinematic universe.
